bib.title: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2024 (38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

read.skipped: References skimmed only; qualitative example figures 9-11 not itemised

question: Can a preference-optimisation objective whose implicit reward is the length-normalised average log-likelihood, with no reference model and a target margin, beat DPO and its variants?
hypothesis: DPO's reward (log ratio to a reference) is mismatched with the average log-likelihood used at generation, which may cause suboptimal performance; aligning them should help.
contributions: SimPO: reference-free, length-normalised reward r=(beta/|y|) log pi(y|x) plus a target reward margin gamma in the Bradley-Terry objective
Comparison to DPO, RRHF, SLiC-HF, IPO, CPO, KTO, ORPO, R-DPO in four setups (Mistral/Llama-3, Base/Instruct) with per-method hyperparameter search
Analysis of length normalisation, margin, reward accuracy, KL and efficiency versus DPO
Gemma-2-9B-it-SimPO model topping AlpacaEval 2 and ranked first among <10B models on Chatbot Arena

method.summary: Offline preference optimisation with loss -log sigma(beta/|yw| log pi(yw|x) - beta/|yl| log pi(yl|x) - gamma), no reference model. Trained on UltraFeedback preferences from Base (Zephyr-style SFT on UltraChat-200k) and Instruct (on-policy regenerated data scored by PairRM) starting points; evaluated on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard and MT-Bench.

datasets.name: UltraFeedback
datasets.split: Base: original chosen/rejected; Instruct: prompts only, responses regenerated
datasets.preprocessing: Instruct setup: 5 responses per prompt from the SFT model at temperature 0.8, scored with llm-blender/PairRM; top-scoring is yw, lowest is yl; single pass, not iterative. Gemma 2 and Llama-3-Instruct v0.2 use RLHFlow/ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1 instead (up to 5 responses per prompt for Gemma)

datasets.name: AlpacaEval 2
datasets.source: Li et al. [55], Dubois et al. [28]

datasets.name: HF Open Leaderboard tasks (MMLU 5, ARC 25, HellaSwag 10, TruthfulQA 0, Winograd 5, GSM8K 5-shot)

training.objective: L_SimPO = -E log sigma( beta/|yw| log pi(yw|x) - beta/|yl| log pi(yl|x) - gamma )
training.lr: SimPO: 3e-7 (Mistral-Base), 5e-7 (Mistral-Instruct), 6e-7 (Llama-3-Base), 1e-6 (Llama-3-Instruct); baselines searched over [3e-7, 5e-7, 6e-7, 1e-6]; SFT stage 2e-5

other.Gemma-2-9B: lr 6e-7, 8e-7 (released), 1e-6 tried; beta and gamma not stated
other.KTO optimiser: Adam used for all, not RMSProp as in KTO paper
other.ORPO: started from same SFT checkpoints as other methods

inference.decoding: AlpacaEval 2: sampling; Arena-Hard: greedy; MT-Bench: official per-category temperatures
inference.temperature: AlpacaEval 2: 0.7 Mistral-Base, 0.5 Mistral-Instruct, 0.9 both Llama-3 (grid-searched over 0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9 for Llama-3-Base with DPO, then fixed for all methods)
inference.samples: one generation per benchmark prompt; run count and seeds not stated

limits: Authors concede no rigorous theory for why SimPO works and that gamma is a new hyperparameter needing manual tuning (App A).
UltraFeedback focuses on helpfulness; safety and honesty not evaluated beyond TruthfulQA (App A).
Preference optimisation, SimPO included, lowers GSM8K and sometimes MMLU, especially with higher learning rates (App A, C, J).
Without KL regularisation SimPO could in principle reward-hack; no collapse seen with proper tuning (Sec 4.4).
No PPO comparison (footnote 7); offline only, no iterative training.
Benchmarks rely on GPT-4 judges, limited query space; MT-Bench differences may be noise.
Gains shrink with a stronger SFT model and higher-quality labels (App H).
Seeds, run counts and total token counts not stated; each method tuned only over small grids.
Hyperparameters beta, gamma are setting-specific (beta 2.0-2.5 but v0.2 uses beta 10, gamma 3).
